Latter with coralline crusts and Caryophyllia common. Very high diversity due to combination of sediment and small shells/cobbles.

LocationName: W of Duisker (east) (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Upper circalittoral cobbles and boulders with muddy coarse sand between, from 18 to 15m bcd. Ophiocomina nigra and Ophiothrix fragilis common. Ciona occasional, Pecten occasional, pink crusts abundant. An unusual feature was the large numbers of Pagurus prideaux and it's commensal anemone. Small Aequipecten were attached to rock surfaces.

LocationName: Central Loch Ceann Dibig (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: A very silty bedrock outcrop on a sediment plain. Brittlestars (Ophiothrix fragilis and Ophiocomina nigra) were common, Ascidia mentula was rare. Some mobile crustacea. Pagurus bernhardus, Hyas araneus, Macropodia rostrata. Sparse hydroids ; Kirchenpaueria pinnata occasional.

LocationName: Cnoc nan Laogh (Loch Leurbost, Lewis)
SampleComment: Soft mud with shell gravel dominated by Ophiothrix fragilis and Ophiocomina nigra. A few small boulders scattered about. Large Cancer pagurus, Asterias rubens, and Echinus esculentus scattered over the area. Boulders mainly covered by encrusting Corallinaceae.

LocationName: Cnoc nan Laogh (Loch Leurbost, Lewis)
SampleComment: Gentle slope from 9 to 6.5m, of soft mud with some shell gravel. Virgularia superabundant, with Liocarcinus, few brittlestars, Callionymus lyra, Gibbula magus, Aequipecten and Mya truncata. Some algal debris and free living Desmarestia aculeata.

LocationName: S of Leurbost (Loch Leurbost, Lewis)
SampleComment: Soft shelly mud with whole shells and occasional small rocky outcrops forming almost level plain at 8.3m bcd. Surprising mixture of epifauna, including Philine aperta, Akera bullata, Ophiodromus, Lunatia catena, Virgularia mirabilis, Ophiothrix fragilis, Antedon bifida and Ophiocomina nigra, many of which were associated with loose red algae lying on the surface of the mud.

LocationName: S of Aird an Tolmachain (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Paguridae, Thyone has been removed from the species list for this record as more specific related taxa were also present, these are now marked as characterising. Mixed coarse sediments, mainly shell gravel and dead maerl but with some coarse sand, stone gravel, pebbles and mud. Fairly varied fauna but nothing in great abundance, including Paguridae, Ophiocomina nigra, Ophiura albida and O. ophiura and holothurians (Thyone spp.). Scattered live maerl.

LocationName: S of Aird an Tolmachain (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Boulders embedded in coarse sediments (habitat 2). Surfaces covered with encrusting coralline algae, brown algae and small patches of Parasmittina. Sparse fauna including Abietinaria abietina, Alcyonium digitata, Psammechinus miliaris, Ophiocomina nigra, Ciona intestinalis and Metridium senile. Slightly shallower areas with Ophiothrix fragilis abundant and very large boulders with colonial diatoms on top.

LocationName: SE Soay MÂ¢r (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Outcrop of bedrock on the lower infralittoral at 12.5 to 14m, grazed by Echinus esculentus. Desmarestia aculeata abundant over most areas with calcareous red and non calc. red crusts. Pawsonia saxicola frequent and Antedon bifida common.

LocationName: Sgeir Reamhar (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Stepped circalittoral bedrock with a covering of silt. Rock surfaces were covered with Pseudolithoderma and coralline crusts. Rock grazed by Echinus esculentus. Antedon bifida was abundant, solitary ascidians (Ascidia mentula and Ciona intestinalis) were frequent. (Habitat not surveyed in detail due to lack of time).

LocationName: Sgeir Linish (Loch Grimshader, Lewis)
SampleComment: Foliose red algae has been given a nominal abundance value of Present for this record as in Arev it had no abundance value. Kelp park of mixed Laminaria hyperborea and Laminaria saccharina on rugged bedrock. Park became much denser in shallower part of zone where it merged indistinctly with forest (habitat 1), and L.saccharina was confined to deeper part of the zone. Foliose algae common on rock which was covered by coralline crusts and Cutleria multifida with many Caryophyllia. Antedon common in patches, particularly on proud parts of rock. Extensive vertical faces were dominated by Corynactis and Antedon, with Pomatoceros and Caryophyllia also common here. Kelp stipes with poor flora, and fronds with Obelia geniculata.

LocationName: Sgeir Linish (Loch Grimshader, Lewis)
SampleComment: Foliose red algae has been given a nominal abundance value of Present for this record as in Arev it had no abundance value. Rugged terrain of bedrock with large fissures and a few pockets of silt/mud with boulders. Upper faces of rock with abundant Caryophyllia on coralline encrusted rock and little other life apart from small patches of algae (Dictyota) in upper part of zone. Steep and vertical faces with more variety, where Ascidia mentula and Cliona were most conspicuous. Antedon in patches on edges of rocks. Thyone roscovita in muddy patches under boulders. Boulders with good populations of cuckoo and goldsinny wrasse and one Homarus gammarus seen.

LocationName: E of Meavaig Island (Loch Leurbost, Lewis)
SampleComment: Gradual slope of soft, very heavily burrowed mud with abundant Virgularia mirabilis and Philine aperta. Burrows not identified but mud surface very irregular with many mounds. Occasional stones with Ophiothrix fragilis, these becoming more frequent further up the slope. Many worm and amphipod tubes in the sediment surface.

LocationName: E of Meavaig Island (Loch Leurbost, Lewis)
SampleComment: Gradual slope of very shelly mud with scattered stones and small boulders. Virgularia mirabilis abundant but becoming less numerous with shallower depth - Ophiothrix fragilis more abundant. Sediment surface solid with amphipod and polychaete tubes. Amphiura spp. becoming more numerous at shallower depths.

LocationName: W Sound of Scalpay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Surfaces of large boulders dominated by encrusting algae but with dense brittlestars (Ophiothrix fragilis and Ophiocomina nigra) overall. Metridium senile present on top of many boulders. Greatest variety of animal species on overhanging surfaces of large boulders at shallowest depths.

LocationName: W Sound of Scalpay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Sandy mud plain covered by Ophiothrix fragilis with Ophiocomina nigra bed. Lots of litter eg. tin cans, old combs, toothbrushes and plastics.

LocationName: W of Eilean Chaluim Chille (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Plain of shelly mud at 22m bcd, with frequent Pennatula phosphorea and frequent Virgularia mirabilis. Many branched mud tubes on the seabed.

LocationName: N of Rubh'an Tanga (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Irregular plain of burrowed mud with Virgularia mirabilis abundant and Philine aperta common. Many tracks and trails in the sediment surface. Some Nephrops burrows, others unidentified. Scattered Ascidiella aspersa lying on sediment surface with small Phyllophora crispa plants attached. Many tubes (amphipods and polychaetes) in mud.

LocationName: SE Eilean Cheois (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Soft mud with some shell gravel and sand. Dominated by Virgularia mirabilis with Thyone fusus and Modiolus modiolus in shallower depths. Common `muddy twiglets' (collected for identification).

LocationName: W of Mâ¦s na Garra (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Steep bedrock in circalittoral with encrusting algae, ascidians and Pomatoceros triqueter. Red algae and Nemertesia ramosa frequent on upward facing surfaces. Upward facing rock very silty.

LocationName: Ard Hurnish, Soay Sound (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Gently sloping bedrock and boulders with a sprinkling of shell gravel, dominated by Ophiura albida and Pomatoceros covered by crustose corallines. The hydroids Abietinaria abietina and Nemertesia antennina were conspicuous on raised or highest rocky ridges.

LocationName: Ard Hurnish, Soay Sound (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Upper infralittoral smooth bedrock with Laminaria hyperborea, not very dense even in shallow water. Long-stiped and with many Echinus grazing. Undergrowth of encrusting coralline algae and Aglaozonia and fairly dense Antedon bifida. Urticina felina and Crossaster paposus frequent. Near the lower limits of kelp where it was sparse, Dictyota dichotoma and Desmarestia aculeata were frequent in the undergrowth, with occasional Halidrys siliquosa. Psammechinus miliaris were also frequent here.

LocationName: Ard Hurnish, Soay Sound (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Upper circalittoral bedrock with encrusting coralline algae and dense Ophiothrix fragilis and Ophiopholis aculeata. Hormathia coronata was rare, Echinus common and Ophiura albida abundant.

LocationName: S Rubha Crago, Sound of Scalpay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Vertical rock face with fissures, dominated by coralline crusts and covered by Antedon bifida. Patches of Corynactis and quite a few Ophiocomina. Fauna more diverse in fissures.

LocationName: S Rubha Crago, Sound of Scalpay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Hydrozoa has been removed from the species list for this record as more specific related taxa were also present, these are now marked as characterising. Steep slope of boulders, some very large (ie. 3m across), on bedrock with sparse kelp park and sparse growth of foliose algae. Rocks quite silty and with quite dense patches of hydroids on algae encrusted rock.

LocationName: S Rubha Crago, Sound of Scalpay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Plain of coarse silty shelly gravel with scattered whole shells, pebbles and cobbles providing attachment for range of hydroids and other epifauna. Chaetopterus and Virgularia in sediment. Quite rich including Antennella, Epizoanthus and Polycarpa fibrosa.

LocationName: Aird Feiltanish (Loch Leurbost, Lewis)
SampleComment: Shelly mud slope from 8 to 13m bcd, with dense bed of Virgularia mirabilis (eighty per square metre). Ophiura ophiura and Amphiura sp. frequent.

LocationName: W of Isay (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: A gradual slope of smooth cobbles and boulders gave way very quickly to sand plain (habitat 2) with a few small bedrock outcrops. Rock and cobbles very smooth and scoured, with algal crusts, Parasmittina trispinora and Abietinaria abietina dominant. Ciona intestinalis frequent.

LocationName: NE tip of Scotasay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Mud with shell gravel and scattered cobbles characterised by Turritella communis and Ophiura ophiura with frequent Cerianthus lloydii and widely scattered Amphiura, Balanus balanus and Nemertesia spp. attached to angular cobbles.

LocationName: NE tip of Scotasay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Ophryotrocha maculata has been given a nominal abundance value of Present for this record as in Arev it had no abundance value. This station extended from the lower infralittoral to upper circalittoral with sediment becoming muddier with depth and with decreasing amount of cobbles. Laminaria saccharina to 16m bcd. Phyllophora crispa in a patchy (10%) band at shallower depths. Aspercoccus turneri and Trailliella extended to 13m bcd.

LocationName: NE of Eilean Arderanish (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Smooth rounded room-sized outcrop of bedrock from sediment of fine mud. Covered with Ophiothrix fragilis and Ophiocomina nigra. Few very large Metridium senile. Rock covered in pink and red crusts, and quite heavily silted. In fissures were Echinus, Ciona, few Alcyonium, Asterias and Pagurus bernhardus.

LocationName: SE of Eilean MÂ¢r Laxay (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Shelly mud plain with some sand, whole and broken shells with superabundant Ocnus planci at 16m bcd (approx. 800 per square metre). Melanella alba (C) conspicuous amongst the O.planci.

LocationName: W Sgeir Ghlas, Scotasay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Plain of muddy fine sand with overlying shell gravel, and some whole shells. Patches of algae on the surface, with a very rich epifauna of Virgularia, Cerianthus, Ophiura spp., Turritella and Gibbula magus.

LocationName: Sound of Scalpay narrows (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Cobbles and boulders embedded in clean shell gravel. Dominated by Ophiothrix fragilis, Ophiocomina nigra and Alcyonium digitata. Young gadoids also present. Strong tidal stream.

LocationName: SE of Isay (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Extensive reef of infralittoral boulders and cobbles resting on sandy substratum, from 8 to 12m bcd. Upper surfaces of the boulders were well grazed and fairly species poor with Desmarestia aculeata and Dictyota dichotoma. By contrast the fauna on the lower boulder surfaces was rich, with lots of Pawsonia saxicola, Galathea squamifera, Chlamys distorta and others.

LocationName: N of Beinn Dhubh (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Rather impoverished habitat of shelly sand and gravel with a scattering of pebbles from 15 to 22m bcd. Ophiocomina and Ophiothrix were moderately dense.

LocationName: N of Beinn Dhubh (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Lower infralittoral kelp park on small boulders, cobbles and pebbles on sand and gravel. Lots of Urticina between the cobbles. The hard surfaces were covered with Dictyota dichotoma and Desmarestia aculeata with occasional Laminaria hyperborea and Laminaria saccharina.

LocationName: W of Gob Aird Stioclett (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Laminaria hyperborea has been given a nominal abundance value of Present for this record as in Arev it had no abundance value. Gently sloping mixture of small and medium sized fairly rounded boulders. Odd larger boulder and mixture of pebbles and shell gravel in small pockets between boulders. All upper surfaces very heavily grazed and dominated by pink crustose algae with brown algae also common. Desmarestia aculeata in dense patches but other foliose algae very sparse excepting Dictyota. Rock surfaces almost devoid of animals with nearly all species (including Pomatoceros and barnacles) confined to undersides where a quite rich growth of spirorbids, encrusting bryozoans, Chlamys spp., Aslia and Pawsonia was present. Sparse park of Laminaria hyperborea with very little growth on stipes.

LocationName: Aird Chaainish (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Slope of bedrock and boulders with dense Laminaria hyperborea and scattered Laminaria saccharina and, at the bottom of the zone, Desmarestia aculeata. Many Pawsonia saxicola between the boulders. Echinus esculentus was abundant in the shallow water, not so numerous deeper, but whole area was fairly heavily grazed.

LocationName: W of Gob Aird Stioclett (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Laminaria hyperborea has been given a nominal abundance value of Present for this record as in Arev it had no abundance value. Gently sloping mixture of small and medium sized fairly rounded boulders. Odd larger boulder and mixture of pebbles and shell gravel in small pockets between boulders. All upper surfaces very heavily grazed and dominated by pink crustose algae with brown algae also common. Desmarestia aculeata in dense patches but other foliose algae very sparse excepting Dictyota. Rock surfaces almost devoid of animals with nearly all species (including Pomatoceros and barnacles) confined to undersides where a quite rich growth of spirorbids, encrusting bryozoans, Chlamys spp., Aslia and Pawsonia was present. Sparse park of Laminaria hyperborea with very little growth on stipes.

LocationName: N of Raarem, South Harbour, Scalpay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Very soft mud with lots of shell debris. Occasional Laminaria saccharina attached to stones. Unidentified worm, possibly Chone spp., common, Sagartiogeton spp. frequent, with occasional Carcinus maenas and rare Sabella pavonina.

LocationName: SW of Cuidsgeir (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Bedrock outcrops from 4 to 10m bcd, with thin covering of silt, covered by dense forest of Laminaria saccharina with some Sacchoriza polyides. Antedon bifida were common on the stipes and fronds of the kelps.

LocationName: SE Hamarsay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Laminaria hyperborea park on mixed large and small boulders and cobbles at 14 to 17m bcd, with dense filamentous and foliose algae on rock surfaces beneath. Trailliella particularly abundant, with Dictyota dichotoma dense in patches. (Dictyota also very dense just below the kelp lower limit, with 100% cover in places on boulders). A variety of other red algae typical of this level(Phycodrys, Bonnemaisonia asparagoides, Kallymenia reniformis).

LocationName: SE Hamarsay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Smooth bedrock outcrops at 24-26m bcd, scoured by and covered with a layer of the surrounding shell gravel. Many large dead barnacle shells. Encrusting dark red and coralline algae on bedrock surfaces and cup corals common. Swiftia pallida conspicuous, and rare Diazona violacea and Porella compressa. On vertical rock near shell gravel, a small patch of Neocrania anomala. Patches of dense spirorbids locally. Possible damage caused by scallop trawls.

LocationName: Bones Rock (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Kelp forest in upper slopes of the Bones Rock pinnacle from 5 to 13m bcd. Laminaria saccharina, L.hyperborea and Saccorhiza polyschides with an understorey of foliose and filamentous reds.

LocationName: Cnoc nan Laogh (Loch Leurbost, Lewis)
SampleComment: Soft mud with shell gravel dominated by Ophiothrix fragilis and Ophiocomina nigra. A few small boulders scattered about. Large Cancer pagurus, Asterias rubens, and Echinus esculentus scattered over the area. Boulders mainly covered by encrusting Corallinaceae.

LocationName: Cnoc nan Laogh (Loch Leurbost, Lewis)
SampleComment: Gentle slope from 9 to 6.5m, of soft mud with some shell gravel. Virgularia superabundant, with Liocarcinus, few brittlestars, Callionymus lyra, Gibbula magus, Aequipecten and Mya truncata. Some algal debris and free living Desmarestia aculeata.

LocationName: Cnoc nan Laogh (Loch Leurbost, Lewis)
SampleComment: Bedrock cliff with vertical and overhanging surfaces covered by encrusting Corallinaceae with Echinus present and clumps of Ascidia mentula descending to fringe of angular boulders with similar biota. All covered over by dense Laminaria saccharina.

LocationName: Sgeir Reamhar (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Plain of shelly gravelly mud with occasional small rocks and whole shells. Would probably have been a very rich habitat before recent scallop dredging activities, which have now given the whole site a `ploughed field' look. Few (R) Pecten, broken Virgularia and Protula turbularia and Rhizocaulus verticillatus on hard substrata. Many other species scattered over the whole habitat, damaged by dredge, eg. Neptunea - broken shells, crabs with missing claws, and half Lanice tubes.

LocationName: Sgeir Linish (Loch Grimshader, Lewis)
SampleComment: Foliose red algae has been given a nominal abundance value of Present for this record as in Arev it had no abundance value. Rugged terrain of bedrock with large fissures and a few pockets of silt/mud with boulders. Upper faces of rock with abundant Caryophyllia on coralline encrusted rock and little other life apart from small patches of algae (Dictyota) in upper part of zone. Steep and vertical faces with more variety, where Ascidia mentula and Cliona were most conspicuous. Antedon in patches on edges of rocks. Thyone roscovita in muddy patches under boulders. Boulders with good populations of cuckoo and goldsinny wrasse and one Homarus gammarus seen.

LocationName: Sgeir Linish (Loch Grimshader, Lewis)
SampleComment: Foliose red algae has been given a nominal abundance value of Present for this record as in Arev it had no abundance value. Fairly dense forest of tall Laminaria hyperborea on bedrock with few large boulders and patches of cobble collected in places. Kelp stipes with Cryptopleura, Palmaria, Membranoptera and some with large colonies of Alcyonium. Fronds with Obelia geniculata and two large stalked jellyfish. Understorey of fairly dense growth of foliose reds, mainly Delesseria on coralline encrusting algae. Corynactis and Caryophyllia present on rock but much less common than in deeper water. Fauna on rocks otherwise sparse. Antedon in patches on rocks and stipes.

LocationName: W Sound of Scalpay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Surfaces of large boulders dominated by encrusting algae but with dense brittlestars (Ophiothrix fragilis and Ophiocomina nigra) overall. Metridium senile present on top of many boulders. Greatest variety of animal species on overhanging surfaces of large boulders at shallowest depths.

LocationName: NE Stanngraidh (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Overhanging bedrock covered by coralline crusts with dense patches of Corynactis. Pomatoceros abundant, few patches of hydroids and Antedon bifida. Not rich.

LocationName: NE Stanngraidh (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Plain of muddy/sandy shell gravel with scattered whole shells/pebbles. Virgularia fairly dense in shallower water, with Amphiura and Cerianthus in shelly sediment. Epifauna attached to stones/shells. Lower sediment plain (below rocky outcrop at 20m) much less diverse.

LocationName: NE Stanngraidh (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Foliose red algae has been given a nominal abundance value of Present for this record as in Arev it had no abundance value. Forest of L.hyperborea from 2 to 4m with band of dense L.saccharina below to 6m on rugged bedrock. Occasional Saccorhiza amongst other kelp. Biota very similar throughout both kelps, with rocks intensely grazed and dominated by coralline crusts. Very few foliose algae (mostly tatty Phycodrys) on rock. Few patches of Antedon, particularly on vertical faces and stipes. L.hyperborea stipes with poor flora of Ptilota, Cryptopleura and Phycodrys.

LocationName: NE Stanngraidh (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Bedrock with sparse Laminaria saccharina park on algae encrusted rock. Caryophyllia abundant but other fauna very sparse. Pawsonia and Neocrania under a single boulder.

LocationName: SE Stockinish Island (Loch Stockinish, Harris)
SampleComment: A vertical bedrock wall overhanging at the top. Rock surface had abundant red algal crusts (coralline and non calcareous). Corynactis viridis was abundant under the overhang, Alcyonium digitatum frequent. At the base of wall Antedon bifida and Caryophyllia smithii were frequent. Encrusting bryozoans and Pomatoceros and Tonicella were also present at the base of the wall. Large Ascidia mentula were frequent, Botryllus schlosseri rare.

LocationName: S Rubha Crago, Sound of Scalpay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Hydrozoa has been removed from the species list for this record as more specific related taxa were also present, these are now marked as characterising. Steep slope of boulders, some very large (ie. 3m across), on bedrock with sparse kelp park and sparse growth of foliose algae. Rocks quite silty and with quite dense patches of hydroids on algae encrusted rock.

LocationName: SE of Urghabeag Bay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Low lying silty bedrock outcropping from sediment slope (Habitat 2 and 4), dominated by brown encrusting algae with Laminaria saccharina and sparse foliose algae. Few Modiolus, but fauna otherwise sparse.

LocationName: NW Riasaidh (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Infralittoral bedrock with large boulders dominated by Laminaria hyperborea and L.saccharina with calcareous pink crusts covering rock surfaces. Turf of foliose red algae on lower section with Pomatoceros spp. and few Caryophyllia. Shoals of two-spotted gobies in the kelp.

LocationName: E Rossay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Ascidiacea has been removed from the species list for this record as more specific related taxa were also present, these are now marked as characterising. A vertical and very steep bedrock cliff from 10 to 15m bcd. Rock surface was grazed and covered with brown and red encrusting algae, encrusting bryozoans and Pomatoceros and Balanus crenatus. Solitary ascidians were frequent. Antedon was common on `edges'. Quite silty.

LocationName: E Rossay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Very steep slope of bedrock with dense Laminaria hyperborea forest from 2 to 8m and kelp park below, giving way to vertical rock face (habitat 2) on to sediment plain (habitat 3). Rock heavily grazed with only sparse red algae, quite heavily silted and covered by algal crusts and barnacles/Pomatoceros. A few large fissures and occasional small boulder. Fauna not rich, with most species present in low density. Kelp stipes devoid of red algae and covered by Filograna, encrusting bryozoans and Antedon. Kelp fronds with many Scrupocellaria reptans

LocationName: SE of Isay (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Extensive reef of infralittoral boulders and cobbles resting on sandy substratum, from 8 to 12m bcd. Upper surfaces of the boulders were well grazed and fairly species poor with Desmarestia aculeata and Dictyota dichotoma. By contrast the fauna on the lower boulder surfaces was rich, with lots of Pawsonia saxicola, Galathea squamifera, Chlamys distorta and others.

LocationName: W Sound of Scalpay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Surfaces of large boulders dominated by encrusting algae but with dense brittlestars (Ophiothrix fragilis and Ophiocomina nigra) overall. Metridium senile present on top of many boulders. Greatest variety of animal species on overhanging surfaces of large boulders at shallowest depths.

LocationName: SW of Cuidsgeir (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Bedrock outcrops from 4 to 10m bcd, with thin covering of silt, covered by dense forest of Laminaria saccharina with some Sacchoriza polyides. Antedon bifida were common on the stipes and fronds of the kelps.

LocationName: N of Raarem, South Harbour, Scalpay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Lower infralittoral sloping bedrock with a heavy covering of fine silt. Patches of red algal turf (covered in silt) with rare small Laminaria saccharina. Ascidia mentula common, with occasional clumps of Cliona celata and Suberites domuncula. Liocarcinus puber and L.depurator occasional. Diatom film in patches.

LocationName: Entrance channel (Loch Grimshader, Lewis)
SampleComment: Gibbula magus has been given a nominal abundance value of Present for this record as in Arev it had no abundance value. Channel floor with pebbles on muddy sand in one area then more open muddy sand with fewer stones in other areas. Dense Laminaria saccharina cover on pebbles, and relatively sparse flora and fauna; sandier areas with less kelp, more Trailliella, shell debris and a wider variety of red and brown algae. Ensis arcuatus frequent in sand.

LocationName: N of Rubh'an Tanga (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Irregular plain of burrowed mud with Virgularia mirabilis abundant and Philine aperta common. Many tracks and trails in the sediment surface. Some Nephrops burrows, others unidentified. Scattered Ascidiella aspersa lying on sediment surface with small Phyllophora crispa plants attached. Many tubes (amphipods and polychaetes) in mud.

LocationName: SE Eilean Cheois (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Shallow sublittoral and sublittoral fringe boulders and cobbles. Dominated by L.saccharina and L.hyperborea. Fairly heavily silted. Vertical and overhanging surfaces under frond canopy dominated by algal crusts with Ascidia mentula in groups of scattered Caryophyllum smithii. Beggiatoa at base of rocks.

LocationName: W of Mâ¦s na Garra (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Steep silty bedrock with dense Laminaria hyperborea to 6m and Laminaria saccharina below this. Thick red algal understorey in shallow parts of the forest. Antedon bifida common on kelp stipes. All very silty.

LocationName: N of Soay MÂ¢r, Soay Sound (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Slope of muddy sand with shell debris, and in deeper parts very large numbers of Turritella communis shells, some live, most dead or with hermit crabs. Ophiura albida common on sediment surface, Chaetopterus variopedatus and Cerianthus lloydii in the sediment. Small tufts of algae attached to shells and Chaetopterus tubes - mostly Plocamium cartilagineum

LocationName: SE Stockinish Island (Loch Stockinish, Harris)
SampleComment: Shelly mud slope with a diatom film over much of the suface and abundant algal debris, including some possibly free-living Phycodrys rubens. Virgularia mirabilis rare. Several Cerianthus lloydii. Many small worm tubes in the sediment, and occasional Amphiura spp.

LocationName: SE Stockinish Island (Loch Stockinish, Harris)
SampleComment: Upper infralittoral bedrock with kelp L.hyperborea and L.saccharina. Rock was vertical leading to very steep and upward facing slope at shallow limit to the habitat. Sparse red algae below kelp. Rock surface had frequent Corynactis viridis and occasional Caryophyllia smithii.

LocationName: Caolas na h-Acarsaid (Loch Mharabhig, Lewis)
SampleComment: Channel floor of muddy shell gravel at 2 to 10m with patchy algal cover, matted together by Trailliella and Audouinella. Peachia cylindrica nearer the rock boundary, several Ensis arcuatus siphons seen.

LocationName: W of Eilean na Gearrabreac (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Gradual slope of muddy shell gravel with small amounts of dead shell. Loose algal mat over much of the area with Trailliella binding gravel. Scinaia turgida frequent. Scattered Virgularia mirabilis and some Pecten maximus.

LocationName: NE tip of Scotasay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: A gentle 15 degree slope of fairly coarse shell gravel with stones and unbroken shells. However digging down into it revealed a fair amount of silt. Algae dominated, particularly Bonnemaisonia asparagoides and Laminaria saccharina. However the diverse flora was only surveyed using samples taken and was incomplete. Animals included Gibbula cineraria, G.magus and Protula tubularia.

LocationName: NE tip of Scotasay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Ophryotrocha maculata has been given a nominal abundance value of Present for this record as in Arev it had no abundance value. This station extended from the lower infralittoral to upper circalittoral with sediment becoming muddier with depth and with decreasing amount of cobbles. Laminaria saccharina to 16m bcd. Phyllophora crispa in a patchy (10%) band at shallower depths. Aspercoccus turneri and Trailliella extended to 13m bcd.

LocationName: NW Riasaidh (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Steep slope of muddy shell gravel becoming progressively shellier with decreasing depth. Patchy cover of loose algal mats bound together by Trailliella and Audouinella. Cerianthus lloydii frequent.

LocationName: W Sgeir Ghlas, Scotasay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Plain of muddy fine sand with overlying shell gravel, and some whole shells. Patches of algae on the surface, with a very rich epifauna of Virgularia, Cerianthus, Ophiura spp., Turritella and Gibbula magus.

LocationName: Loch nam Bodach (Loch nam Bodach, Lewis)
SampleComment: Mainly boulders and cobbles at 0 to 2m below loch datum, with a few areas of vertical bedrock with clear zonation. Fucus serratus was present around loch datum, with Laminaria saccharina and scattered Halidrys siliquosa below 0.2m bld. Rock surfaces were covered with dense Trailliella in places in shallow water. Halidrys and L.saccharina had many Ascidiella aspersa and Scrupocellaria sp. epiphytic, with Anemonia viridis frequent near the entrance channel and sill between the two basins. Gobius niger (very large) also frequent near the sill, Gobiusculus flavescens locally. On vertical bedrock, a very pronounced zonation described on the site sheet.

LocationName: SE Hamarsay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Dense Laminaria hyperborea on a steep bedrock slope at 5-6m bcd. Kelp plants of two sizes, an upper layer of long-stiped old plants and an understorey of small plants. Rock surfaces with a short undergrowth of Scrupocellaria sp. with scattered red algae and Dictyota dichotoma. Kelp stipes with many red algae, very tattered and covered with Crisia eburnea.

LocationName: Channel between Ardteaginish and Or Eilean, Scalpay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Gradual slope of boulders and cobbles on coarse muddy sand and shell gravel. Shore dominated by Fucus vesiculosus and Ascophyllum nodosum with some Fucus serratus and frequent patches of filamentous green algae. Rocks beneath the algae very silty with few additional algae species. Variety of animals under boulders and in overhangs.

LocationName: NE Stanngraidh (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Rugged bedrock with Laminaria digitata, Alaria esculenta(R) and foliose red algae.

LocationName: NE Stanngraidh (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Bedrock dominated by barnacles (Balanus balanoides) with Nucella lapillus super abundant. Young Mytilus common, with Actinia equina locally abundant in crevices and fissures. Fucus vesiculosus in patches.

LocationName: Risay Causeway (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Band of Fucus serratus with Mastocarpus on rugged bedrock with understorey of Semibalanus.

LocationName: Sgeir Linish (Loch Grimshader, Lewis)
SampleComment: Foliose red algae has been given a nominal abundance value of Present for this record as in Arev it had no abundance value. Fairly dense forest of tall Laminaria hyperborea on bedrock with few large boulders and patches of cobble collected in places. Kelp stipes with Cryptopleura, Palmaria, Membranoptera and some with large colonies of Alcyonium. Fronds with Obelia geniculata and two large stalked jellyfish. Understorey of fairly dense growth of foliose reds, mainly Delesseria on coralline encrusting algae. Corynactis and Caryophyllia present on rock but much less common than in deeper water. Fauna on rocks otherwise sparse. Antedon in patches on rocks and stipes.

LocationName: Aird Chaainish (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Slope of bedrock and boulders with dense Laminaria hyperborea and scattered Laminaria saccharina and, at the bottom of the zone, Desmarestia aculeata. Many Pawsonia saxicola between the boulders. Echinus esculentus was abundant in the shallow water, not so numerous deeper, but whole area was fairly heavily grazed.

LocationName: Tanneray (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Moderately exposed bedrock, vertical/very steep in places characterised by Balanus balanoides (100% cover). Patella vulgata were abundant and Nucella lapillus common, especially in fissures. Small Mytilis edulis were frequent in damp places: crevices/fissures etc.. Sparse algae - stunted specimens.

LocationName: W of Mâ¦s na Garra (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Steep silty bedrock with dense Laminaria hyperborea to 6m and Laminaria saccharina below this. Thick red algal understorey in shallow parts of the forest. Antedon bifida common on kelp stipes. All very silty.

LocationName: Caolas na h-Acarsaid (Loch Mharabhig, Lewis)
SampleComment: Steep bedrock slope with boulder at its base dominated by Laminaria hyperborea shallower and L. saccharina deeper. Algal crusts abundant on vertical surfaces. Red and brown algae frequent on upward facing rock and kelp stipes. All very silty.

LocationName: Shore opposite Brutha Sgeir (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Lower shore with Fucus serratus covered with Ascidiella scabra with Laminaria digitata just below.

LocationName: Ardteaginish ob narrows, Scalpay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Wide band of dense Ascophyllum nodosum on steep boulder slope. Fauna and flora under Ascophyllum very sparse, but under boulder fauna quite rich with numerous Dendrodoa and bryozoan crusts.

LocationName: SE of loch (Loch Stockinish, Harris)
SampleComment: Lower eulittoral bedrock with dense Fucus serratus, with Elachista and Palmaria epiphitic. Laurencia pinnatifida and Mastocarpus stellatus both frequent, and a small variety of other red algae beneath the Fucus and in crevices. Himanthalia elongata occasional. Predominantly Semibalanus balanoides over rock but with common Balanus crenatus.

LocationName: SE of loch (Loch Stockinish, Harris)
SampleComment: Shaded vertical and overhanging rock formed by large boulders characterised by encrusting Corallinaceae with associated Spirorbis corallinae, large patches of Umbonula littoralis, scattered Polyclinum aurantium, Botrylloides leachi and Grantia compressa. Urticina felina on vertical rock but more abundant in fissures at base.(Sub-habitat of 031.005.004)

LocationName: SE of loch (Loch Stockinish, Harris)
SampleComment: Lower eulittoral bedrock with abundant Laminaria digitata and Fucus serratus common. Encrusting brown algae in large patches amonst barnacles. A small variety of other algae. Animals include Umbonula littoralis and Polychinum aurantium with a fairly small variety of other species.

LocationName: W Sgeir Ghlas, Scotasay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Very dense forest of L. hyperborea on bedrock with few boulders collected in the hollows. Rock very heavily grazed with very little fauna or foliose algae, except under boulders. Kelp fronds with Obelia geniculata, Scrupocellaria reptans and Spirorbis. Stipes with tatty flora including Ptilota, Membranipora, Cryptopleura and Palmaria.

LocationName: Shore, Gob Aird na Cille, Scalpay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Mid eulittoral broken bedrock with dense Balanus balanoides and common Fucus vesiculosis, mainly without bladders. Elachista epiphytic on Fucus fronds, and Dynamena and Alcyonidium hirsutum amongst bases.

LocationName: Shore, Gob Aird na Cille, Scalpay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Steep bedrock ridges on lower eulittoral of exposed shore with Himanthalia elongata and Mastocarpus stellatus between 1.5 and 2.0m acd. Also Balanus balanoides, Amphilectus fucorum, Halichondria panicea and rare Botryllus schlosseri under the Himanthalia

LocationName: Shore, Gob Aird na Cille, Scalpay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Broken bedrock in the sublittoral fringe, at 1 to 1.5m acd. Laminaria digitata abundant, over encrusting coralline algae, encrusting brown algae, barnacles, Umbonula littoralis and a wide variety of other animal and plant species. Crevices with Sagartia elegans and small Urticina felina. Helcion pellucidum frequent on Laminaria fronds.

LocationName: Shore, Gob Aird na Cille, Scalpay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Steep walled surge gully opening out at the lower shore. Zonation pattern on walls, from 3m to 1m acd : barnacles/fucoids ; Palmaria palmata ; Plumaria elegans and Lomentaria ; Umbonula, coralline red algae and Botryllus schlosseri. Very similar to lower shore zonation pattern.

LocationName: Sound of Scalpay narrows (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Vertical and overhanging shaded tide-swept rock on the lower shore characterised by Sarsia eximia and Alcyonium digitata with Corynactis viridis and Sagartia elegans present. Dominant cover of encrusting Corallinaceae but Umbonula littoralis has high cover. Large variety of species present.

LocationName: W of Gob Aird Stioclett (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Gentle slope of slightly rugged bedrock with some patches of boulders. Fairly open forest of Laminaria hyperborea with sparse flora on stipes; Membranipora on fronds. Rock very highly grazed by Echinus and dominated by coralline crusts, with Desmarestia and Dictyota reasonably common (but less dense than in deeper water). Fauna very sparsely with virtually no sessile species on upper rock faces. Under boulder fauna similar to habitat 2 but much fewer boulders at this shallower depth.

LocationName: Central basin (Loch Stockinish, Harris)
SampleComment: Angular boulders with vertical and steeply sloping surfaces colonised by Pomatocerus triqueter and Caryophyllia smithii with scattered Echinus esculentus and Antedon bifida. Large solitary Metridium senile present at the tops of rocks. There were almost certainly other species present but adverse conditions prevented a full survey.

LocationName: S Rubha Crago, Sound of Scalpay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Plain of coarse silty shelly gravel with scattered whole shells, pebbles and cobbles providing attachment for range of hydroids and other epifauna. Chaetopterus and Virgularia in sediment. Quite rich including Antennella, Epizoanthus and Polycarpa fibrosa.

LocationName: Shore, Gob Aird na Cille, Scalpay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Steep bedrock ridges on lower eulittoral of exposed shore with Himanthalia elongata and Mastocarpus stellatus between 1.5 and 2.0m acd. Also Balanus balanoides, Amphilectus fucorum, Halichondria panicea and rare Botryllus schlosseri under the Himanthalia

LocationName: Shore of Brutha Sgeir (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Small channel with strong tide running over it. Floor of mixed boulders, cobbles and pebbles on muddy gravel. Laminaria digitata dominant. Numerous Ascidiella scabra and Ascidia conchilega on the algae and beneath boulders. Rich lower shore fauna and flora but not completely searched due to limited time available.

LocationName: E Rossay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Ascidiacea has been removed from the species list for this record as more specific related taxa were also present, these are now marked as characterising. A vertical and very steep bedrock cliff from 10 to 15m bcd. Rock surface was grazed and covered with brown and red encrusting algae, encrusting bryozoans and Pomatoceros and Balanus crenatus. Solitary ascidians were frequent. Antedon was common on `edges'. Quite silty.

LocationName: E Rossay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Very steep slope of bedrock with dense Laminaria hyperborea forest from 2 to 8m and kelp park below, giving way to vertical rock face (habitat 2) on to sediment plain (habitat 3). Rock heavily grazed with only sparse red algae, quite heavily silted and covered by algal crusts and barnacles/Pomatoceros. A few large fissures and occasional small boulder. Fauna not rich, with most species present in low density. Kelp stipes devoid of red algae and covered by Filograna, encrusting bryozoans and Antedon. Kelp fronds with many Scrupocellaria reptans

LocationName: S Rubha Crago, Sound of Scalpay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Plain of coarse silty shelly gravel with scattered whole shells, pebbles and cobbles providing attachment for range of hydroids and other epifauna. Chaetopterus and Virgularia in sediment. Quite rich including Antennella, Epizoanthus and Polycarpa fibrosa.

LocationName: Sound of Scalpay narrows (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Current-swept steep infralittoral bedrock, with kelp forest at 7m bcd and lowest kelp at 18m bcd. Undergrowth of dense erect bryozoans, mainly Scrupocellaria sp. and Crisidia cornuta. Erect hydroids also frequent, particularly Eucratea loricata, Abietinaria abietina and Rhizocaulus verticillatus. Sagartia elegans abundant. Drifts of mobile shell gravel on gullies, with a few Cerianthus lloydii and sand gobbies.

LocationName: Narrows to inner loch (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Ophiura has been removed from the species list for this record as more specific related taxa were also present, these are now marked as characterising. Extensive plain of muddy sediment with admixture of shelly gravel, fine sand and stones. Virgularia, Pennatula and Amphiura in sediment with numerous polychaete tubes erect from surface. Ophiura ophiura and O.albida frequent on surface, together with wide variety of other animals including Hero formosa, Erato voluta and Melanella alba. Scattered shells and cobbles provided attachment for a range of hydroids, particularly Kirchenpaueria and Nemertesia spp., with clumps of Abietinaria on larger rocks. Latter with coralline crusts and Caryophyllia common. Very high diversity due to combination of sediment and small shells/cobbles.

LocationName: W of Duisker (east) (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Sand with mud from 24 to 18m bcd dominated by Amphiura filiformis with Ophiura ophiura and O.albida. Cerianthus lloydii and Thyone fusus more common in shallower part of habitat. Hermit crabs and Aequipecten common and frequent respectively. Several mollusc shells with Adamsia carciniopados but without hermit crabs. Visibility only about 1m near sediment surface.

LocationName: W of Duisker (east) (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Upper circalittoral cobbles and boulders with muddy coarse sand between, from 18 to 15m bcd. Ophiocomina nigra and Ophiothrix fragilis common. Ciona occasional, Pecten occasional, pink crusts abundant. An unusual feature was the large numbers of Pagurus prideaux and it's commensal anemone. Small Aequipecten were attached to rock surfaces.

LocationName: Cnoc nan Laogh (Loch Leurbost, Lewis)
SampleComment: Soft mud with shell gravel dominated by Ophiothrix fragilis and Ophiocomina nigra. A few small boulders scattered about. Large Cancer pagurus, Asterias rubens, and Echinus esculentus scattered over the area. Boulders mainly covered by encrusting Corallinaceae.

LocationName: Risay Causeway (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Band of Fucus serratus with Mastocarpus on rugged bedrock with understorey of Semibalanus.

LocationName: S of Aird an Tolmachain (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Paguridae, Thyone has been removed from the species list for this record as more specific related taxa were also present, these are now marked as characterising. Mixed coarse sediments, mainly shell gravel and dead maerl but with some coarse sand, stone gravel, pebbles and mud. Fairly varied fauna but nothing in great abundance, including Paguridae, Ophiocomina nigra, Ophiura albida and O. ophiura and holothurians (Thyone spp.). Scattered live maerl.

LocationName: S of Aird an Tolmachain (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Boulders embedded in coarse sediments (habitat 2). Surfaces covered with encrusting coralline algae, brown algae and small patches of Parasmittina. Sparse fauna including Abietinaria abietina, Alcyonium digitata, Psammechinus miliaris, Ophiocomina nigra, Ciona intestinalis and Metridium senile. Slightly shallower areas with Ophiothrix fragilis abundant and very large boulders with colonial diatoms on top.

LocationName: Sgeir Linish (Loch Grimshader, Lewis)
SampleComment: Foliose red algae has been given a nominal abundance value of Present for this record as in Arev it had no abundance value. Kelp park of mixed Laminaria hyperborea and Laminaria saccharina on rugged bedrock. Park became much denser in shallower part of zone where it merged indistinctly with forest (habitat 1), and L.saccharina was confined to deeper part of the zone. Foliose algae common on rock which was covered by coralline crusts and Cutleria multifida with many Caryophyllia. Antedon common in patches, particularly on proud parts of rock. Extensive vertical faces were dominated by Corynactis and Antedon, with Pomatoceros and Caryophyllia also common here. Kelp stipes with poor flora, and fronds with Obelia geniculata.

LocationName: E of Meavaig Island (Loch Leurbost, Lewis)
SampleComment: Gradual slope of soft, very heavily burrowed mud with abundant Virgularia mirabilis and Philine aperta. Burrows not identified but mud surface very irregular with many mounds. Occasional stones with Ophiothrix fragilis, these becoming more frequent further up the slope. Many worm and amphipod tubes in the sediment surface.

LocationName: E of Meavaig Island (Loch Leurbost, Lewis)
SampleComment: Gradual slope of very shelly mud with scattered stones and small boulders. Virgularia mirabilis abundant but becoming less numerous with shallower depth - Ophiothrix fragilis more abundant. Sediment surface solid with amphipod and polychaete tubes. Amphiura spp. becoming more numerous at shallower depths.

LocationName: Entrance channel (Loch Grimshader, Lewis)
SampleComment: Gibbula magus has been given a nominal abundance value of Present for this record as in Arev it had no abundance value. Channel floor with pebbles on muddy sand in one area then more open muddy sand with fewer stones in other areas. Dense Laminaria saccharina cover on pebbles, and relatively sparse flora and fauna; sandier areas with less kelp, more Trailliella, shell debris and a wider variety of red and brown algae. Ensis arcuatus frequent in sand.

LocationName: W of Tannaraidh (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Amphiura chiajei/filiformis has been given a nominal abundance value of Present for this record as in Arev it had no abundance value. Extensive plain of soft mud with shell fragments and many stones, plus occasional cobble or small boulder on the surface. Pennatula common; Amphiura sp., O.ophiura and Chaetopterus frequent. Caryophyllia and Epizoanthus attached to subsurface stones. Boulders and cobbles provide attachment for Caryophyllia, Neocrania and Leptometra. Few large burrows, Luidia sarsi and Anseropoda present (one of each seen).

LocationName: Ard Hurnish, Soay Sound (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Gently sloping bedrock and boulders with a sprinkling of shell gravel, dominated by Ophiura albida and Pomatoceros covered by crustose corallines. The hydroids Abietinaria abietina and Nemertesia antennina were conspicuous on raised or highest rocky ridges.

LocationName: Ard Hurnish, Soay Sound (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Upper infralittoral smooth bedrock with Laminaria hyperborea, not very dense even in shallow water. Long-stiped and with many Echinus grazing. Undergrowth of encrusting coralline algae and Aglaozonia and fairly dense Antedon bifida. Urticina felina and Crossaster paposus frequent. Near the lower limits of kelp where it was sparse, Dictyota dichotoma and Desmarestia aculeata were frequent in the undergrowth, with occasional Halidrys siliquosa. Psammechinus miliaris were also frequent here.

LocationName: SE of Am Maoladh (Loch Stockinish, Harris)
SampleComment: Large outcrop of bedrock with occasional patch of angular boulder. Quite silty and with occasional large fissure. Extensive vertical rock on one side of outcrop (habitat 2). Top of rock with fairly dense cape L. hyperborea and thick carpet of Trailliella, with much thinner kelp below to rock/sediment interface. Here rock covered by algal crusts with frequent solitary ascidians, especially Ascidia mentula, and Antedon bifida. Foliose algae not common. Under-boulders quite rich with bryozoan crusts, ascidians and Pomatoceros. Kelp stipes very bare except Filograna and occasionally A. digitata, with only Electra, and Obelia geniculata on fronds.

LocationName: Ardteaginish ob narrows, Scalpay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Fringe of Laminaria digitata on boulders with rich underboulder community, particularly bryozoan crusts, crisiidae and colonial ascidians.

LocationName: S Rubha Crago, Sound of Scalpay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Hydrozoa has been removed from the species list for this record as more specific related taxa were also present, these are now marked as characterising. Steep slope of boulders, some very large (ie. 3m across), on bedrock with sparse kelp park and sparse growth of foliose algae. Rocks quite silty and with quite dense patches of hydroids on algae encrusted rock.

LocationName: N of Bogh'a'Chaolais (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Soft muddy slope (gentle, 10 degrees at most). Dominant were Virgularia forming a`forest` over all area studied. Also on sediment Ophiura albida, Ophiura ophiura, Philine aperta and Inachus dorsettensis were conspicuous. A few large vertical burrows and one Nephrops burrow seen.

LocationName: W of Isay (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: A gradual slope of smooth cobbles and boulders gave way very quickly to sand plain (habitat 2) with a few small bedrock outcrops. Rock and cobbles very smooth and scoured, with algal crusts, Parasmittina trispinora and Abietinaria abietina dominant. Ciona intestinalis frequent.

LocationName: NE of Eilean Arderanish (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Smooth rounded room-sized outcrop of bedrock from sediment of fine mud. Covered with Ophiothrix fragilis and Ophiocomina nigra. Few very large Metridium senile. Rock covered in pink and red crusts, and quite heavily silted. In fissures were Echinus, Ciona, few Alcyonium, Asterias and Pagurus bernhardus.

LocationName: W Sgeir Ghlas, Scotasay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Very dense forest of L. hyperborea on bedrock with few boulders collected in the hollows. Rock very heavily grazed with very little fauna or foliose algae, except under boulders. Kelp fronds with Obelia geniculata, Scrupocellaria reptans and Spirorbis. Stipes with tatty flora including Ptilota, Membranipora, Cryptopleura and Palmaria.

LocationName: W Sgeir Ghlas, Scotasay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Dense canopy of Laminaria saccharina with occasional L. hyperborea and Saccorhiza on steepish slope of bedrock and boulders. Lower part of forest mainly boulders with patches of silty shell gravel between. Rocks very heavily grazed and covered by algal crusts with very few foliose algae or fauna. Under-boulders had most of the fauna seen, and was dominated by bryozoan crusts. Spirorbis and Gibbula cineraria were abundant on kelp fronds.

LocationName: SE of Isay (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Extensive reef of infralittoral boulders and cobbles resting on sandy substratum, from 8 to 12m bcd. Upper surfaces of the boulders were well grazed and fairly species poor with Desmarestia aculeata and Dictyota dichotoma. By contrast the fauna on the lower boulder surfaces was rich, with lots of Pawsonia saxicola, Galathea squamifera, Chlamys distorta and others.

LocationName: Narrows to inner loch (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Ophiura has been removed from the species list for this record as more specific related taxa were also present, these are now marked as characterising. Extensive plain of muddy sediment with admixture of shelly gravel, fine sand and stones. Virgularia, Pennatula and Amphiura in sediment with numerous polychaete tubes erect from surface. Ophiura ophiura and O.albida frequent on surface, together with wide variety of other animals including Hero formosa, Erato voluta and Melanella alba. Scattered shells and cobbles provided attachment for a range of hydroids, particularly Kirchenpaueria and Nemertesia spp., with clumps of Abietinaria on larger rocks. Latter with coralline crusts and Caryophyllia common. Very high diversity due to combination of sediment and small shells/cobbles.

LocationName: SW of Cuidsgeir (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Plain of firm shelly mud at 10m bcd. Modiolus modiolus was present in clumps, with Mya truncata and Circomphalus casina. Fairly high species richness.

LocationName: SE of Ardvey (Loch Stockinish, Harris)
SampleComment: Very soft mud plain from 4-8m BCD, with a few burrows. No particularly dominant species except gobies (Pomatoschistus sp.) which were everywhere! Scattered Mya were conspicuous.

LocationName: W of Eilean Thoraidh (Loch Mharabhig, Lewis)
SampleComment: A sediment slope composed of soft mud with shell and stone gravel. A lot of drift algae and scattered empty shells. Common gobies with occasional Pholis and Myoxocephalus. Mud burrowed by crabs - Cancer and Liocarcinus depurator. Sparse infauna : Cerianthus lloydii was common. Ophiura albida (common) and O.ophiura (occasional) present on the surface.

LocationName: W of Tannaraidh (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Amphiura chiajei/filiformis has been given a nominal abundance value of Present for this record as in Arev it had no abundance value. Extensive plain of soft mud with shell fragments and many stones, plus occasional cobble or small boulder on the surface. Pennatula common; Amphiura sp., O.ophiura and Chaetopterus frequent. Caryophyllia and Epizoanthus attached to subsurface stones. Boulders and cobbles provide attachment for Caryophyllia, Neocrania and Leptometra. Few large burrows, Luidia sarsi and Anseropoda present (one of each seen).

LocationName: S Rubha Crago, Sound of Scalpay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Plain of coarse silty shelly gravel with scattered whole shells, pebbles and cobbles providing attachment for range of hydroids and other epifauna. Chaetopterus and Virgularia in sediment. Quite rich including Antennella, Epizoanthus and Polycarpa fibrosa.

LocationName: Aird Feiltanish (Loch Leurbost, Lewis)
SampleComment: Shelly mud slope from 8 to 13m bcd, with dense bed of Virgularia mirabilis (eighty per square metre). Ophiura ophiura and Amphiura sp. frequent.

LocationName: Aird Feiltanish (Loch Leurbost, Lewis)
SampleComment: Slope of mud with large proportion of shell gravel and a few pebbles and shells. Dense foliose and filamentous algae, mainly Dictyota dichotoma and Asperococcus turneri and filamentous reds (Trailliella/Rhodochorton). Scattered Chorda filum and Laminaria saccharina.

LocationName: SE of Urghabeag Bay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Low lying silty bedrock outcropping from sediment slope (Habitat 2 and 4), dominated by brown encrusting algae with Laminaria saccharina and sparse foliose algae. Few Modiolus, but fauna otherwise sparse.

LocationName: SE of Urghabeag Bay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Extensive muddy plain with some shells and scattered surface shell debris. Sparse epifauna of Modiolus (1 or 2 clumps only) and Ascidiella aspersa (2 to 3 per clump) with Cerianthus and Mya in sediment. Philine fairly frequent on surface. Modiolus/A.aspersa declining in numbers with depth as sediment became muddier and had a few vertical burrows at greater depth.

LocationName: SE Soay MÂ¢r (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Maerl collected in troughs of low lying waves on a plain of shelly coarse firm sand. Many dead shells (Glycymeris and Dosinia) on the surface providing attachment for tufts of foliose algae, mainly Rhodomela and Brongniartella. Neopentadactyla, Thyone fusus, Cerianthus and Ensis sp. frequent in sediment. Anapagurus chiroacanthus and Ophiura albida common on the surface, with a few Pecten.

LocationName: Bones Rock (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Vertical bedrock wall from 13m to 21.5m bcd, with Corynactis viridis and Antedon bifida on the lower portion, Hormathia occasionally, and a few foliose algae at 13m, mainly Dictyota dichotoma.

LocationName: SE of Isay (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Plain of coarse and medium sand, with some gravel and pebbles from 11 to 13m bcd, dominated by Ensis sp.. Modiolus were also common in patches. The habitat appeared to be a nursery area for Pecten maximus which were common but all small.

LocationName: North Harbour, Scalpay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Lichens has been given a nominal abundance value of Present for this record as in Arev it had no abundance value. Upper shore bedrock encompassing the lichen zone and Pelvetia canaliculata zone. Both groups were abundant. Sparse fauna : a few amphipods and occasional Littorina saxatilis.

LocationName: NE Stanngraidh (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Supralittoral fringe bedrock dominated by yellow, grey and black lichens.

LocationName: NW Eilean MÂ¢r Laxay (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Upper littoral fringe dominated by Verrucaria maura with Lichina confinis and spots of yellow and grey lichens.

LocationName: SE Bunavoneadar (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Supralittoral lichens on bedrock at 4.9 to 5.9m above chart datum. Loch surface with >90% cover of lichens, black lichens characterising the lower half of the zone, grey and yellow lichens characterising the upper half.

LocationName: Tanneray (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: A broad supralittoral/littoral fringe zone, with 100% cover of lichens. Verrucaria maura was abundant on the littoral. Ramalina and Xanthoria were supralittoral species while Calloplaca spp. were more common in the littoral fringe. Littorina neritoides and L. saxatilis were common.

LocationName: Shore opposite Brutha Sgeir (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Supralittoral yellow and grey lichens with Verrucaria maura.

LocationName: SE of loch (Loch Stockinish, Harris)
SampleComment: Broken rock on upper shore with narrow band of grey and yellow (Calloplaca marina) lichens above black lichens and scattered Pelvetia, the latter mainly growing in crevices on flatter rocks. Many Littorina saxatilis in the lower part of the zone.

LocationName: Shore, Gob Aird na Cille, Scalpay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Bedrock with crevices and fissures with grey and yellow lichens. Verrucaria maura (60%=abundant), Grey lichens (15%), Lichina confinis, Calloplaca and Littorina saxatilis in crevices.

LocationName: Narrows to inner loch (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Ophiura has been removed from the species list for this record as more specific related taxa were also present, these are now marked as characterising. Extensive plain of muddy sediment with admixture of shelly gravel, fine sand and stones. Virgularia, Pennatula and Amphiura in sediment with numerous polychaete tubes erect from surface. Ophiura ophiura and O.albida frequent on surface, together with wide variety of other animals including Hero formosa, Erato voluta and Melanella alba. Scattered shells and cobbles provided attachment for a range of hydroids, particularly Kirchenpaueria and Nemertesia spp., with clumps of Abietinaria on larger rocks. Latter with coralline crusts and Caryophyllia common. Very high diversity due to combination of sediment and small shells/cobbles.

LocationName: W of Duisker (east) (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Bedrock with pink crusts, Parasmittina trispinosa and Desmarestia viridis. Thin turf of filamentous red algae. Fissures and crevices with Ciona, Cliona, Calliostoma and Kirchenpaueria. 15m bcd to 13m bcd - may have been continued on shallows, but not surveyed on this dive.

LocationName: Bones Rock (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Vertical bedrock wall from 13m to 21.5m bcd, with Corynactis viridis and Antedon bifida on the lower portion, Hormathia occasionally, and a few foliose algae at 13m, mainly Dictyota dichotoma.

LocationName: Bones Rock (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Large boulder-slope between 21.5 and 27.5m bcd, with patches of sediment in between. Ciona intestinalis dominant on rock with Nemertesia ramosa and Nemertesia antennina and abundant Caryophyllia smithii. Also Swiftia pallida, Leptometra celtica and Cliona celata.

LocationName: SE Soay MÂ¢r (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Maerl collected in troughs of low lying waves on a plain of shelly coarse firm sand. Many dead shells (Glycymeris and Dosinia) on the surface providing attachment for tufts of foliose algae, mainly Rhodomela and Brongniartella. Neopentadactyla, Thyone fusus, Cerianthus and Ensis sp. frequent in sediment. Anapagurus chiroacanthus and Ophiura albida common on the surface, with a few Pecten.

LocationName: SE Soay MÂ¢r (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Outcrop of bedrock on the lower infralittoral at 12.5 to 14m, grazed by Echinus esculentus. Desmarestia aculeata abundant over most areas with calcareous red and non calc. red crusts. Pawsonia saxicola frequent and Antedon bifida common.

LocationName: Sgeir Reamhar (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Plain of shelly gravelly mud with occasional small rocks and whole shells. Would probably have been a very rich habitat before recent scallop dredging activities, which have now given the whole site a `ploughed field' look. Few (R) Pecten, broken Virgularia and Protula turbularia and Rhizocaulus verticillatus on hard substrata. Many other species scattered over the whole habitat, damaged by dredge, eg. Neptunea - broken shells, crabs with missing claws, and half Lanice tubes.

LocationName: Sgeir Reamhar (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Stepped circalittoral bedrock with a covering of silt. Rock surfaces were covered with Pseudolithoderma and coralline crusts. Rock grazed by Echinus esculentus. Antedon bifida was abundant, solitary ascidians (Ascidia mentula and Ciona intestinalis) were frequent. (Habitat not surveyed in detail due to lack of time).

LocationName: Sgeir Linish (Loch Grimshader, Lewis)
SampleComment: Foliose red algae has been given a nominal abundance value of Present for this record as in Arev it had no abundance value. Rugged terrain of bedrock with large fissures and a few pockets of silt/mud with boulders. Upper faces of rock with abundant Caryophyllia on coralline encrusted rock and little other life apart from small patches of algae (Dictyota) in upper part of zone. Steep and vertical faces with more variety, where Ascidia mentula and Cliona were most conspicuous. Antedon in patches on edges of rocks. Thyone roscovita in muddy patches under boulders. Boulders with good populations of cuckoo and goldsinny wrasse and one Homarus gammarus seen.

LocationName: W Sound of Scalpay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Surfaces of large boulders dominated by encrusting algae but with dense brittlestars (Ophiothrix fragilis and Ophiocomina nigra) overall. Metridium senile present on top of many boulders. Greatest variety of animal species on overhanging surfaces of large boulders at shallowest depths.

LocationName: W of Eilean Thoraidh (Loch Mharabhig, Lewis)
SampleComment: Rhodophycota indet.(non-calc.crusts) has been given a nominal abundance value of Present for this record as in Arev it had no abundance value. A bedrock and large boulder outcrop on a sediment plain. Rock heavily silted, many organisms were smothered. Rock was heavily grazed by Echinus. Scattered, very large L. saccharina plants. Solitary ascidians were abundant, mainly A. aspera with some A. mentula, A. conchilega and A. scabra. Common juvenile gadoids, leopard spotted gobies and sparse red algae. Bonnemaionia asparagoides occasional.

LocationName: W of Eilean Thoraidh (Loch Mharabhig, Lewis)
SampleComment: A sediment slope composed of soft mud with shell and stone gravel. A lot of drift algae and scattered empty shells. Common gobies with occasional Pholis and Myoxocephalus. Mud burrowed by crabs - Cancer and Liocarcinus depurator. Sparse infauna : Cerianthus lloydii was common. Ophiura albida (common) and O.ophiura (occasional) present on the surface.

LocationName: SE Eilean Cheois (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Shell mud with some shell gravel from 5.5 to 10m bcd. Laminaria saccharina rare, with Trailliella, Asperococcus, Gibbula magus, Ulva, Anemonia viridis, Dictyota dichotoma. Scattered clumps of Modiolus modiolus.

LocationName: SE Eilean Cheois (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Soft mud with some shell gravel and sand. Dominated by Virgularia mirabilis with Thyone fusus and Modiolus modiolus in shallower depths. Common `muddy twiglets' (collected for identification).

LocationName: NE Stanngraidh (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Overhanging bedrock covered by coralline crusts with dense patches of Corynactis. Pomatoceros abundant, few patches of hydroids and Antedon bifida. Not rich.

LocationName: W of Mâ¦s na Garra (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Steep bedrock in circalittoral with encrusting algae, ascidians and Pomatoceros triqueter. Red algae and Nemertesia ramosa frequent on upward facing surfaces. Upward facing rock very silty.

LocationName: W of Mâ¦s na Garra (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Gradual slope of muddy shell gravel and sand with scattered algae, frequent Cerianthus lloydii. Some Pecten maximus and pebbles, both with hydroids and barnacles attached. Occassional small Vigularia mirabilis.

LocationName: W of Mâ¦s na Garra (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Steep silty bedrock with dense Laminaria hyperborea to 6m and Laminaria saccharina below this. Thick red algal understorey in shallow parts of the forest. Antedon bifida common on kelp stipes. All very silty.

LocationName: N of Soay MÂ¢r, Soay Sound (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: The bottom of a bedrock slope, broken by patches of shell gravel (habitat 2), with an open kelp forest of Laminaria hyperborea and some Halidrys siliquosa. Antedon bifida frequent, some hydroids present, and patches of Sagartia elegans and Metridium senile.

LocationName: N of Soay MÂ¢r, Soay Sound (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Band of shell gravel between bedrock and muddy sand (Habitat 3), and shell gravel patches amongst bedrock. Not surveyed in detail due to lack of time. Sporochnus pedunculatus present, Pecten maximus, Gibbula magus, Thyone fusus and Thyone roscovita.

LocationName: Ard Hurnish, Soay Sound (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: A gentle to moderate slope of sediment leading from rocky outcrops and boulders. Pecten shells and Chaetopterus tubes formed an important substratum for the attachment of surface dwellers eg. hydroids. Ophiura ophiura and Ophiura albida were conspicuous and Chlamys varia frequent. Thyone fusus were common in the sediment, with rare Neopentadactyla.

LocationName: SE of Am Maoladh (Loch Stockinish, Harris)
SampleComment: Large outcrop of bedrock with occasional patch of angular boulder. Quite silty and with occasional large fissure. Extensive vertical rock on one side of outcrop (habitat 2). Top of rock with fairly dense cape L. hyperborea and thick carpet of Trailliella, with much thinner kelp below to rock/sediment interface. Here rock covered by algal crusts with frequent solitary ascidians, especially Ascidia mentula, and Antedon bifida. Foliose algae not common. Under-boulders quite rich with bryozoan crusts, ascidians and Pomatoceros. Kelp stipes very bare except Filograna and occasionally A. digitata, with only Electra, and Obelia geniculata on fronds.

LocationName: W of Eilean na Gearrabreac (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Ophiura ophiura and small crabs seemed the dominant conspicuous species including Inachus dorsettensis, Pagurus bernhardus and Anapagurus. The sediment showed signs of disturbance, with areas looking like they had been gauged out. The observation of several scallop dredgers operating in the area led to suspicions that the habitat had extensive dredge damage. Virgularia was very patchy and few burrows or scallops were noted.

LocationName: S Rubha Crago, Sound of Scalpay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Hydrozoa has been removed from the species list for this record as more specific related taxa were also present, these are now marked as characterising. Steep slope of boulders, some very large (ie. 3m across), on bedrock with sparse kelp park and sparse growth of foliose algae. Rocks quite silty and with quite dense patches of hydroids on algae encrusted rock.

LocationName: E Tabhaidh MhÂ¢r (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: A fairly steep slope of muddy shell gravel with Chaetopterus and Pennatula being the most conspicuous species. The Chaetopterus tubes act as a substratum for hydroids etc. as did the odd stone. Apart from these species, habitat was pretty bare. Several specimens eg. Porania pulvillus looked as if they had come from elsewhere - presumably the rock above.

LocationName: W of Isay (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: A gradual slope of smooth cobbles and boulders gave way very quickly to sand plain (habitat 2) with a few small bedrock outcrops. Rock and cobbles very smooth and scoured, with algal crusts, Parasmittina trispinora and Abietinaria abietina dominant. Ciona intestinalis frequent.

LocationName: NE of Eilean Arderanish (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Fine silty mud at 15 to 15.5m bcd, with some shells and shell fragments on bedrock and in deeper pockets. Ophiura albida and O.ophiura present throughout, with occasional/rare clumps of approximately 5 to 10 Modiolus modiolus. Turritella communis common over most of the muddy sediments, and both Buccinum undatum and Neptunea antiqua occasional.

LocationName: NE of Eilean Arderanish (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Smooth rounded room-sized outcrop of bedrock from sediment of fine mud. Covered with Ophiothrix fragilis and Ophiocomina nigra. Few very large Metridium senile. Rock covered in pink and red crusts, and quite heavily silted. In fissures were Echinus, Ciona, few Alcyonium, Asterias and Pagurus bernhardus.

LocationName: W of Duisker (east) (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Upper circalittoral cobbles and boulders with muddy coarse sand between, from 18 to 15m bcd. Ophiocomina nigra and Ophiothrix fragilis common. Ciona occasional, Pecten occasional, pink crusts abundant. An unusual feature was the large numbers of Pagurus prideaux and it's commensal anemone. Small Aequipecten were attached to rock surfaces.

LocationName: Braigh MÂ¢r (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Smooth silty bedrock dominated by encrusting Corallinacea with abundant Parasmittina trispinosa, Swiftia pallida and Caryophyllia smithii. Shallow depth have fairly dense algae and some dense Antedon bifida at ridges. (Antedon and Balanus balanus generally found only occasionally but are dense in places - Antedon bifida on a ridge in the lower infralittoral, Balanus balanus near the rock-sediment interface).

LocationName: Central Loch Ceann Dibig (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: A very silty bedrock outcrop on a sediment plain. Brittlestars (Ophiothrix fragilis and Ophiocomina nigra) were common, Ascidia mentula was rare. Some mobile crustacea. Pagurus bernhardus, Hyas araneus, Macropodia rostrata. Sparse hydroids ; Kirchenpaueria pinnata occasional.

LocationName: Bones Rock (Loch Erisort, Lewis)
SampleComment: Vertical bedrock wall from 13m to 21.5m bcd, with Corynactis viridis and Antedon bifida on the lower portion, Hormathia occasionally, and a few foliose algae at 13m, mainly Dictyota dichotoma.

LocationName: S of Aird an Tolmachain (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Boulders embedded in coarse sediments (habitat 2). Surfaces covered with encrusting coralline algae, brown algae and small patches of Parasmittina. Sparse fauna including Abietinaria abietina, Alcyonium digitata, Psammechinus miliaris, Ophiocomina nigra, Ciona intestinalis and Metridium senile. Slightly shallower areas with Ophiothrix fragilis abundant and very large boulders with colonial diatoms on top.

LocationName: N of Raarem, South Harbour, Scalpay (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Lower infralittoral sloping bedrock with a heavy covering of fine silt. Patches of red algal turf (covered in silt) with rare small Laminaria saccharina. Ascidia mentula common, with occasional clumps of Cliona celata and Suberites domuncula. Liocarcinus puber and L.depurator occasional. Diatom film in patches.

SampleComment: Plain of shelly gravelly mud with occasional small rocks and whole shells. LocationName: Sgeir Reamhar (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Stepped circalittoral bedrock with a covering of silt. Rock surfaces were covered with Pseudolithoderma and coralline crusts. Rock grazed by Echinus esculentus. Antedon bifida was abundant, solitary ascidians (Ascidia mentula and Ciona intestinalis) were frequent. (Habitat not surveyed in detail due to lack of time).

SampleComment: Foliose red algae has been given a nominal abundance value of Present for this record as in Arev it had no abundance value. LocationName: E of Meavaig Island (Loch Leurbost, Lewis)
SampleComment: Gradual slope of very shelly mud with scattered stones and small boulders. Virgularia mirabilis abundant but becoming less numerous with shallower depth - Ophiothrix fragilis more abundant. Sediment surface solid with amphipod and polychaete tubes. Amphiura spp. becoming more numerous at shallower depths.

LocationName: SE of Ardvey (Loch Stockinish, Harris)
SampleComment: Laminaria saccharina forest from 1m ACD to 2m BCD on very large and large boulders. Rocks silty and covered with Balanus crenatus. Gibbula cineraria very common.

SampleComment: Rhodophycota indet.(non-calc.crusts) has been given a nominal abundance value of Present for this record as in Arev it had no abundance value. LocationName: W of Mâ¦s na Garra (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Steep bedrock in circalittoral with encrusting algae, ascidians and Pomatoceros triqueter. Red algae and Nemertesia ramosa frequent on upward facing surfaces. Upward facing rock very silty.

LocationName: W of Mâ¦s na Garra (East Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Gradual slope of muddy shell gravel and sand with scattered algae, frequent Cerianthus lloydii. Some Pecten maximus and pebbles, both with hydroids and barnacles attached. Occassional small Vigularia mirabilis.

SampleComment: The bottom of a bedrock slope, broken by patches of shell gravel (habitat 2), with an open kelp forest of Laminaria hyperborea and some Halidrys siliquosa. Antedon bifida frequent, some hydroids present, and patches of Sagartia elegans and Metridium senile.

LocationName: Ard Hurnish, Soay Sound (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Gently sloping bedrock and boulders with a sprinkling of shell gravel, dominated by Ophiura albida and Pomatoceros covered by crustose corallines. The hydroids Abietinaria abietina and Nemertesia antennina were conspicuous on raised or highest rocky ridges.

LocationName: Ard Hurnish, Soay Sound (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Upper infralittoral smooth bedrock with Laminaria hyperborea, not very dense even in shallow water. Long-stiped and with many Echinus grazing. Undergrowth of encrusting coralline algae and Aglaozonia and fairly dense Antedon bifida. Urticina felina and Crossaster paposus frequent. Near the lower limits of kelp where it was sparse, Dictyota dichotoma and Desmarestia aculeata were frequent in the undergrowth, with occasional Halidrys siliquosa. Psammechinus miliaris were also frequent here.

LocationName: Caolas na h-Acarsaid (Loch Mharabhig, Lewis)
SampleComment: Channel floor of muddy shell gravel at 2 to 10m with patchy algal cover, matted together by Trailliella and Audouinella. Peachia cylindrica nearer the rock boundary, several Ensis arcuatus siphons seen.

LocationName: NW Bo Harainish (West Loch Tarbert, Harris)
SampleComment: Very soft fine mud from 17 to 13m bcd. Asterias rubens abundant and Philine aperta common. Mounds and burrows occasional, plus tubes of 1mm diameter (amphipods ?) common. Anapagurus chiroacanthus frequent, Pagurus bernhardus occasional.

LocationName: SE of Am Maoladh (Loch Stockinish, Harris)
SampleComment: Large vertical rock face on an outcrop, dominated by Ciona, with patches of Antedon bifida. Dictyota dichotoma.

LocationName: SE of Am Maoladh (Loch Stockinish, Harris)
SampleComment: Large outcrop of bedrock with occasional patch of angular boulder. Quite silty and with occasional large fissure. Extensive vertical rock on one side of outcrop (habitat 2). Top of rock with fairly dense cape L. hyperborea and thick carpet of Trailliella, with much thinner kelp below to rock/sediment interface.
